nodes.summary: A *pairing* of a finite set $X$ is a fixed-point-free involution of $X$: a map $s:X\to X$ with $s(x)\ne x$ and $s(s(x))=x$ for all $x\in X$, that is, a partition of $X$ into pairs. The number of pairings of $X$ is odd if $|X|$ is even and even if $|X|$ is odd. For distinct $x,y\in X$, the pairings $s$ of $X$ with $s(x)=y$ correspond bijectively to the pairings of $X\setminus\{x,y\}$.
nodes.title: Pairings are odd in number exactly on sets of even size
